note: Research snapshot of pending Australian AI regulatory developments. Every item is a watch item, not an obligation. Confirm each against its primary source at use time; policai.org is a discovery index only.

watch_items.item: Legislated 'Australian Standards for AI' and Office of AI
watch_items.status_at_snapshot: Announced 15 July 2026; Office of AI established in PM&C; legislation targeted early 2027; confirmed scope so far limited to large-AI-data-centre requirements and creator-consent copyright protections; National Cabinet outcome not yet published at the snapshot (the 26 August 2026 communique is now on pm.gov.au)
watch_items.expected_trigger: PM&C consultation outcome, exposure draft or Bill introduction (targeted early 2027)
watch_items.status_at_review: No exposure draft or Bill located. National Cabinet's 26 August 2026 communique and the Prime Minister's 15 July 2026 release both still say the Commonwealth intends to legislate in early 2027; the communique records agreement to develop nationally consistent mandatory standards for large data centres (energy, water, land use), and commentary (not the communique) reports that a renewables requirement was not agreed. PM&C's consultation 'Getting it right: Building AI infrastructure that works for Australia' ran 18 September to 9 October 2026 and its insights were published on 13 November 2026 (see pmc-ai-infrastructure-consultation). That consultation covers conditions for training AI models, but PM&C states that copyright policy is outside its scope and is led by the Attorney-General, so the creator-consent copyright limb in the 15 July announcement should be treated as unsettled. A reported (leaked) Attorney-General's Department paper floating an opt-out model rests on secondary sources
watch_items.review_basis: pm.gov.au release and National Cabinet communique, and pmc.gov.au consultation page, read on 2026-11-16

watch_items.item: OAIC guidance on transparency in automated decision making
watch_items.status_at_snapshot: Consultation issues paper 18 May 2026, submissions closed 15 June 2026; final guidance expected before the APP 1.7-1.8 commencement on 10 December 2026
watch_items.status_at_review: Final guidance published 30 Sep 2026: APP Guidelines chapter 1 (Version 2.0, updated 30 Sep 2026), linking an APP 1.7-1.9 Transparency Obligation fact sheet, a supplementary fact sheet for government agencies and a flowchart. Reported (secondary sources) themes: 'computer program' read broadly (rule-based tools, spreadsheets and generative AI included); human review does not take a tool out of scope where its output is a material input to the decision; the duty sits with the entity that arranges the use, not the vendor; the commercial-in-confidence carve-out is narrow. Guidance only, not law; APP 1.7-1.9 apply from 10 Dec 2026. The watch item can close once the guidance is reflected in the privacy skills
watch_items.review_basis: OAIC chapter 1 page, media release and consultation page (updated 16 Oct 2026) read on 2026-11-02; the three PDFs and the guideline's substance were not read. Read the current chapter before quoting it

watch_items.item: ASX Corporate Governance Council Principles and Recommendations, 5th edition
watch_items.status_at_snapshot: Draft in consultation (July 2026); verified negative: the draft contains no AI-specific recommendation, only generic material-risk disclosure; 4th edition (2019) remains in force; 5th edition targeted at financial years commencing on or after 1 July 2027
watch_items.expected_trigger: Recommendation of the final 5th edition to the ASX board (expected December 2026) and final publication
watch_items.status_at_review: Consultation on the draft fifth edition closed 14 September 2026. The ASX Corporate Governance Council Advisory Group met on 12 October 2026, anticipates recommending changes to the ASX Board in early December 2026 and next meets on 24 November 2026. The fourth edition remains in effect until ASX notifies otherwise. The first reporting periods and the absence of an AI-specific recommendation recorded at the snapshot are not stated on the page or the communique and were not re-verified against the draft
watch_items.review_basis: asx.com.au corporate governance page and the 13 October 2026 Advisory Group communique read on 2026-11-16

watch_items.item: Possible appeal from the ART's Bunnings decision of 4 February 2026
watch_items.status_at_snapshot: ART affirmed APP 1 and APP 5 findings, set aside APP 3.3 under s 16A; OAIC noted an appeal period applies; neutral citation to be located on AustLII before formal citation

Reported neutral citation: Bunnings Group Ltd and Privacy Commissioner (Guidance and Appeals Panel) [2026] ARTA 130 — reported, verify on AustLII before citing. Candidate for retirement once confirmed

watch_items.item: Second tranche of Privacy Act reform
watch_items.status_at_snapshot: Government commitment only; Attorney-General confirmed in February 2026 Senate estimates that a tranche 2 Bill is being progressed; no Bill introduced, no timetable
watch_items.status_at_review: The Attorney-General's Department consultation page confirms that the Exposure Draft Privacy Amendment (Personal Data Protection) Bill 2026 was released on 31 August 2026 and that the consultation closed on 18 September 2026; it says the Bill 'remains subject to further consideration by government'. No Bill introduction was confirmed either way: the Parliament bills list could not be filtered reliably. The proposal details recorded at the snapshot were not re-verified against the exposure draft
watch_items.review_basis: consultations.ag.gov.au privacy reform page read on 2026-11-16

watch_items.item: PM&C consultation 'Getting it right: Building AI infrastructure that works for Australia'
watch_items.status_at_snapshot: Not on the register at the 14 August 2026 snapshot
watch_items.expected_trigger: Consultation close (reportedly 9 October 2026) and any resulting exposure draft of the Australian Standards for AI
watch_items.status_at_review: Closed 5 pm AEDT Friday 9 Oct 2026. On 13 Nov 2026 PM&C published 'Public consultation insights', recording 1,533 submissions and a five-stage process (consultation, evidence base, standards development, government consideration, introduction of standards) ending with 'Australia's AI standards to be released'. It gives no date, exposure draft or Bill. The consultation page says copyright policy is outside the consultation's scope and is led by the Attorney-General; the insights page nonetheless reports that 64% of submissions addressed copyright and AI training data and that views diverged. Feeds the development of the Australian Standards for AI (see standards-for-ai-bill)
watch_items.review_basis: pmc.gov.au news item and consultation page read on 2026-11-16; the insights page read on the same day from a copy the maintainer downloaded (the site blocks automated access)
